short_definition: Deceptive communication designed to trick individuals into revealing sensitive information or credentials.
layman_explanation: Sending a fake email pretending to be your bank so you log in and give away your password.

short_definition: A targeted phishing attack tailored specifically to an individual or organization using personal context.
layman_explanation: An email customized with your boss's name and recent project details asking you to sign an urgent doc.

short_definition: A specialized phishing attack targeting high-profile executives like C-suite leaders.
layman_explanation: A fake legal summons sent directly to a CEO to trick them into transferring corporate funds.

short_definition: Voice phishing conducted over phone calls to manipulate victims into sharing confidential data.
layman_explanation: A scam caller posing as tech support asking you to read out a 2FA code sent to your phone.

short_definition: Phishing attacks delivered via SMS or text messages containing malicious links.
layman_explanation: A text message claiming a package delivery failed and urging you to tap a link to update your address.

short_definition: Registering domain names with common misspellings of popular sites to trick mistyping users.
layman_explanation: Registering 'goolge.com' hoping you mistype 'google.com' and land on a fake login screen.

short_definition: Creating a fabricated scenario to persuade a target to release information or perform an action.
layman_explanation: An attacker pretending to be an auditor conducting a drill so you hand over internal files.

short_definition: Offering an enticing promise or physical object to lure a victim into a security trap.
layman_explanation: Leaving a USB drive labeled 'Executive Salaries 2026' in a parking lot for someone to plug in.

short_definition: Requesting information in exchange for a promised service or benefit.
layman_explanation: An attacker calling employees pretending to fix an IT glitch if they provide their passwords first.

short_definition: Following an authorized person into a physically restricted area without credentials.
layman_explanation: Walking closely behind an employee holding coffee cups so they hold the badge door open for you.

short_definition: Gaining physical entry with the explicit consent of an authorized person under false pretenses.
layman_explanation: Asking an employee to hold the secure door because you claim you forgot your badge in your car.

short_definition: Directly observing someone's screen or keypad to capture passwords, PINs, or data.
layman_explanation: Watching someone type their ATM PIN or laptop password from behind them in a crowded café.

short_definition: Rummaging through trash to locate discarded sensitive documents, passwords, or hardware.
layman_explanation: Searching a company's recycle bins for unshredded papers containing customer phone numbers.

short_definition: Compromising a website frequently visited by a target group to infect their devices.
layman_explanation: Infecting a local restaurant menu site known to be visited daily by employees of a nearby firm.

short_definition: Phishing using malicious QR codes that redirect targets to credential-stealing websites.
layman_explanation: Placing a fake QR code sticker on a parking meter that opens a fraudulent payment site.

short_definition: Spoofing customer support accounts on social media to intercept complaints and credentials.
layman_explanation: An attacker replying to your tweet complaining to an airline, offering a fake refund link.

short_definition: A scam where attackers impersonate corporate figures to trick staff into sending funds.
layman_explanation: An attacker emailing an accountant using a lookalike address to request an immediate wire payment.

short_definition: Using search engine optimization to push fraudulent sites to the top of search results.
layman_explanation: Making a fake customer care site rank first on Google so victims call the scammer's hotline.

short_definition: Copying a legitimate previously sent email and swapping the attachment or link with malware.
layman_explanation: Resending a real company update email you received yesterday, but replacing the PDF with malware.

short_definition: Creating fake romantic or personal personas to manipulate targets into handing over secrets.
layman_explanation: Creating a fake dating profile to flirt with an engineer and trick them into sharing company code.

short_definition: Tactics designed to shock users into purchasing rogue anti-virus software.
layman_explanation: A flashing pop-up stating 'Your computer is infected with 83 viruses! Click here to clean now.'

short_definition: Impersonating IT or major software technicians to gain remote access to a victim's machine.
layman_explanation: A pop-up warning your computer is locked and telling you to call a fake Microsoft help line.

short_definition: Using AI-generated synthetic voice or video to convincingly impersonate executives or relatives.
layman_explanation: Cloning a manager's voice using AI to call an employee and authorize an urgent money transfer.

short_definition: Tricking users into granting OAuth app permissions to third-party malicious applications.
layman_explanation: A pop-up asking 'Allow cool app to read your emails?' that secretly exposes your inbox to hackers.

short_definition: Rewriting the contents of an unattended browser tab to display a fake login page.
layman_explanation: Leaving a tab open while away, and coming back to find it transformed into a fake Gmail login prompt.

short_definition: Creating a problem so the victim reaches out to the attacker for help.
layman_explanation: Sabotaging a network printer and leaving a business card so staff call you to 'fix' it.

short_definition: Altering the address bar text in a browser to make a malicious site look legitimate.
layman_explanation: Displaying 'bank.com' in the URL field even though the page is hosted on a scammer's server.

short_definition: Redirecting website traffic to a bogus site by poisoning local DNS or host files.
layman_explanation: Typing 'paypal.com' correctly, but being secretly sent to a fake site due to tampered router settings.

short_definition: Sending fake billing statements to companies hoping finance teams pay without auditing.
layman_explanation: Mailing a fake $400 office supply invoice to a firm expecting someone will just approve it.

short_definition: Manipulating public social narratives to compromise executive credibility or manipulate stock.
layman_explanation: Spreading coordinated bot rumors about a company breach to induce panicking shareholders.

short_definition: Luring targets onto rogue Wi-Fi networks using familiar access point names.
layman_explanation: Setting up a free hotspot named 'Starbucks_Guest' across the street to capture user activity.

short_definition: Systematically collecting user passwords and credentials through large-scale lure campaigns.
layman_explanation: Setting up 50 lookalike university login pages to collect thousands of student passwords.

short_definition: An open-source framework designed to perform simulated social engineering attacks.
layman_explanation: A toolkit security professionals use to test if employees fall for fake phishing emails.

short_definition: Bombarding a target with repeated multi-factor push notifications until they approve out of frustration.
layman_explanation: Sending 50 login approval prompts at 3 AM until the sleepy target clicks 'Approve' to stop it.

short_definition: Tricking users into clicking invisible buttons overlaid on attractive content.
layman_explanation: Clicking a play button on a viral video that actually triggers a hidden 'Follow' or 'Buy' button.

short_definition: Pretending to be another specific individual to gain trust or access.
layman_explanation: Putting on an Amazon delivery vest to walk past building security unchecked.

short_definition: Leveraging fake managerial status to compel obedience without question.
layman_explanation: Demanding immediate file transfers by stating 'I'm VP of Operations and don't have time for red tape.'

short_definition: Creating artificial time pressure so targets act emotionally rather than logically.
layman_explanation: Stating 'Your account will be permanently deleted in 15 minutes unless you click here now.'

short_definition: Manipulating individuals by showing fake evidence that peers have already complied.
layman_explanation: Telling an employee 'All other regional managers have already submitted their passwords, you're last.'

short_definition: Building rapport through charm and common interests before making malicious requests.
layman_explanation: Chatting up a receptionist about sports teams for a week before asking for internal directory access.

short_definition: Promoting limited availability to spur quick, unconsidered user compliance.
layman_explanation: Offering 'Only 3 free security upgrades left for employees today' to trigger fast clicks.

short_definition: An email notification that lacks malicious links but urges the victim to phone a scam center.
layman_explanation: An email confirming a fake $900 subscription charge that says 'Call this number if you didn't authorize.'

short_definition: Scammers demanding payment specifically in retail gift card codes to evade tracking.
layman_explanation: A fake boss emailing you to buy $500 in Apple gift cards for a client presentation right now.

short_definition: Adopting the visual styling, logos, and voice of well-known brands to deceive targets.
layman_explanation: Designing a fake email that matches Netflix's exact colors to report a 'failed membership payment.'

short_definition: Using short audio samples to synthetically replicate a family member or coworker's voice.
layman_explanation: Calling parents using a synthesized voice of their child claiming they lost their wallet while traveling.

short_definition: Promising rewards for completing online surveys to collect personally identifiable information.
layman_explanation: Fill out this 5-question survey to win an iPhone, but first enter your address and SSN.

short_definition: Sending a bad check for more than expected and asking the target to refund the difference.
layman_explanation: Sending a $1,000 check for a $200 item and asking you to wire back the $800 'mistake' before the check bounces.

short_definition: Establishing fake emotional relationships over long periods to exploit victims financially.
layman_explanation: Building trust over months online then fabricating emergency medical expenses requiring money wires.
